lines: I ask the sky vaguely through the classroom window.
"Why am I alive?" I don't know.
I'm forced to learn only things I never wanted to know.
When I realized it, I'd even lost my own words.
The ideal me I wrote in the textbook margins.
I'm not just obeying the adults.
There is a freedom like that of a soaring bird.
They showed us dreams but gave us no power to make them come true.
Not giving us that, it only makes things painful.
Even the length of a skirt is set for us.
Unable to do what I want, where am I?
A voice inside my heart says, "I'm here."
Even though the sky is beautiful.
